name: Power Rail Tree
blurb: supply rails as a tree with each branch's current budget and total power
intro: List each source, regulator and load with the rail it hangs from. Currents are summed from the leaves up: an LDO draws its output current from its parent, a switcher draws Vout·Iout/(η·Vin), so every branch shows its current, its loss and how close it is to its rating.

inputs.label: Rails, regulators and loads
inputs.help: Parent is the name of the rail it is fed from (empty for a source). Load A is current drawn directly from this rail by things not listed as rows. Efficiency applies to switchers only. For a load row, V is ignored (it runs at its parent's voltage).

examples.title: 12 V board: 5 V buck, 3.3 V LDO, a motor on the input rail
Li-ion cell: 1.8 V core LDO and a 5 V boost

usage: Pass rails as an array of rows {name, parent, type: source|switcher|ldo|load, v (volts out), load (amps drawn directly on this rail), limit (regulator or source rating in amps), eff (switcher efficiency in percent)}. Numbers may be strings with engineering prefixes ("120m"). It returns, per node, output and input current, power and loss and the use of its rating (also as result.tree in depth-first order), plus total input power, delivered power, losses and efficiency; warnings flag over-rated regulators, LDO dropout and hot LDOs. Use it for a board power budget or to size a regulator or input connector.
sources: Energy balance: switcher Iin = Vout·Iout / (η·Vin); linear regulator Iin = Iout (quiescent current neglected), loss (Vin−Vout)·Iout - e.g. TI SLVA079 'Understanding the terms and definitions of LDO voltage regulators' and TI SLVA477 (buck power stage)
80 % continuous-use derating is a common design rule of thumb
